hints: The lowest common ancestor is the deepest node that is an ancestor of both query nodes.
Lift the deeper node until both nodes have equal depth.
Then jump both upward from largest powers down whenever their ancestors differ; their parent is the LCA.
analogy: Bring two employees to the same management level, then raise them together until just before their paths meet.
example: If nodes 4 and 5 share parent 2, their lowest common ancestor is 2.
algorithm: Precompute depths and binary ancestors. Equalize depths, lift both by powers of two while ancestors differ, then return parent of either.
correctness: After equalizing depth, the nodes remain below their LCA; lifting them together while keeping ancestors distinct stops exactly at its children.
complexity: O(n log n+q log n) time and O(n log n) space.
